L15: cite9†View PDF cite10†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:In this paper we use ideas introduced earlier by Moody, Long, Long-Paton, and Bigelow to prove the theorem of the title, that the Burau representation of the classical braid group is faithful for n = 4. An immediate corollary is that the Jones representation of the braid group is also faithful for n = 4.

L30@P0: The braid groups are the most remarkable groups from topological point of view naturally appearing
L31@P0: in the theory of knots, mapping class groups and configuration spaces; see [8]. They were explicitly
L32@P0: introduced by Emil Artin in 1925 [3], who denoted their n-strand versions by Bn. The (Artin) braid group
L33@P0: Bn is generated by n − 1 elements σ1, ... , σn−1 with braid relations
